        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p>System tools are built-in features that help Optimizely Opal take action. Each tool performs a specific task, such as creating a campaign, uploading files, or generating images. Think of tools like attachments on a Swiss Army knife. Each one has a distinct purpose that helps you get work done.</p><p>In addition to the <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/39340107628429" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">system tools available in Opal</a>, Optimizely Content Management System (CMS) (SaaS) includes a set of system tools to help you with CMS-related tasks, such as managing content.</p><div class="note">Ask Opal what tools it has at any time. For example, enter <em>"Please list the tools you have with a brief description of what they do and the parameters"</em> into <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Opal Chat</a>.</div><p>Click a tool's name to expand it and learn when to use it, its required and optional parameters, and example prompts for calling the tool. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.</p><h2 id="h_01K5W6R30FHS5TSMTC84131WBX">Content types<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K5W6R30FHS5TSMTC84131WBX"></a></h2><p><a href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/content-types-saas#/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Content types</a> act as blueprints for your content, specifying what kind of data each piece of content can hold. For example, a "News Article" content type might have fields for title, body, author, and publish date.</p><details><summary><code>cms_list_content_types</code> – Gets a list of content types, excluding properties, from CMS (SaaS). This tool provides an overview of the available content structures you can use, without providing the full details of each property.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="efa278cfd688eab94491937ce387757ed">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eba70b8eeff008d9ed35296c9d02f84bb">See all the content types that are available in your CMS (SaaS) instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8d059993e4fac2a69ef1ee240621c36b">Understand the different kinds of content you can create or manage.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9fe8a91e75cb2989298eb0679cee7faa">Identify content types before performing actions like creating new content, getting detailed information about a specific content type (using <code>cms_get_content_type_details</code>), or creating a new content type (using <code>cms_create_content_type</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed8f086b7c2b53a743cc62a7013a9163e">Filter content types by their base type (for example, to see only pages or only components).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed5b42029b97c12c806f89247e8dcc870">
<strong>Properties</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="ed6b07ed94bcb2c3357ed34a84a09d84d">(Optional) <code>BaseType</code> – Filter the list of content types by their base type. If you do not provide a  <code>BaseType</code>, the tool returns all content types. Valid values include the following: <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e825721b3d12dd37588ee445525824405">
<code>_page</code> </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e87ad5b7deeee2fb8c30fd8fcf6987fc1"><code>_experience</code></li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8a407b2bc97b0ffb5868b0fdbb130867"> <code>_component</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e32f8837df650970cf55a57c3ae6bfc78"> <code>_media</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1c1550ab894050d077b1b9b4fc479abb"> <code>_image</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e85b4845e9e0560facb70c28cb2f467f3"> <code>_video</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec0658c7c33fa6b3b02e042a8daafcd08"> <code>_section</code>
</li>
</ul>
</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e3691da006f4f43382d00e018ef8ab296">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e91f31d0a5350e87a81a9113f42364615"><em>List all content types in my CMS (SaaS) instance.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e30f7e1d9cb1a3741968562023e4cd24e"><em>What content types are available?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8eb13841a4dd86f684b85b204e34329c"><em>Show me all the page content types.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e4b09d2e376330d6120caa7d5542e952b"><em>Can you list all the component content types?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed3dca274b149a0af2b72eeb73b1a2c74"><em>What media content types do we have?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_get_content_type_details</code> – Gets the full details of a content type, including properties, from CMS (SaaS).</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e29fdb392abb8a896de93c9f9364765d2">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e950b8966a59e850e757057c464e806a1">Inspect the complete structure and configuration of an existing content type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2f4c6983d0d9df19a3f0f1e1e8804472">Understand all the fields (properties) defined for a content type, their types, and other settings.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb87dcf46d6b7d3f9181161331cd770dd">Get detailed information about a content type after listing them with the <code>cms_list_content_types</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e966435d6b0a597f08847571eb5997059">Review a content type's definition before making updates with <code>cms_update_content_type</code> or creating new content based on it.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e05b4cc34412a204ea63044a2cdd64a75">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e426c6fca523251fcb00abb03a917dff9">
<code>ContentTypeKey</code> – The unique machine-readable key for an existing content type in your CMS (SaaS) instance.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e67422a57895b213f5dd00c03585508d4">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e6d2b2e2329e946bd75f42821005476ff"><em>Get the full details for the 'Article' content type.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0831f5dddccce7b7d00a4304e691655a"><em>Show me all the properties of the content type with the key 'ProductPage'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e90ca32e1c26945da4dcd808735170759"><em>Can you provide the complete schema for the 'HeroComponent' content type?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_create_content_type</code> – Creates a new content type in CMS (SaaS).</summary><div class="important"><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ebde8f1f47885a72796470619bb0a9cdf">New content types must follow the same conventions (for example, naming conventions) as existing content types. Use the <code>cms_list_content_types</code> tool to get existing content types and the <code>cms_get_content_type_details</code> tool to get details, including all properties for a specific content type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e990dc02f191c98565486ebcacc0fb156">If you are creating multiple content types, always create and register content types with <code>baseType: "_component"</code> first. This ensures that other content types can properly reference them.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ead05f9df893e1891051f9e083c9f9d76">The <code>group</code> field for a property must reference an existing property group. Use the <code>cms_list_property_groups</code> tool to list existing property groups or the <code>cms_create_property_group</code> tool to create one. See the <a href="#h_01K8XJ5H66WA32H2T126Y5YJ7Y">Property groups</a> section.</li>
</ul></div>
<ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eef0d96b58e084daf573a662b3f6dd4a9">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e621aa2a1efc94f20e18f70060f959c25">Define a new structure for a specific type of content you want to manage in your CMS (SaaS) instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64eebe322cae60668227a8d9ed8cac41">Create content models for pages, experiences, components, or sections.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec5d4018ca30b57f440c1bde820b7f510">Standardize the properties and behaviors of content items across your website or application.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eff8d8606301ec6edce6861817fa120f3">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e2d30961885b398cedf110743b0aae0ea">
<code>Key</code> – A machine-readable key that must be unique in your instance of CMS (SaaS) (for example, 'NewsArticle', 'HeroComponent').</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efc49958386d352095c312673dbe14ad7">
<code>DisplayName</code> – The human-readable name of the content type (for example, 'News Article', 'Hero').</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb163d36f8f32e448078f3ba0041b4521">
<code>Description</code> – A brief explanation of the content type's purpose (for example, 'Used to display news articles on a website').</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e20956d6b2f91dfce1e7068b6a282d621">
<code>BaseType</code> – The base type of the content type. Valid values include the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e3b12cc868211b17b77c0e8a55f678500">
<code>_page</code> – For content that has a fixed position in your site structure and a specific URL (e.g., an "About Us" page).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e96528359dd0706ed1089f5c3f3422cc7">
<code>_experience</code> – Similar to <code>_page</code>, but includes a dynamic area where editors can add components and sections.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5c5bc4228d840983cecd2651c29294d7">
<code>_component</code> – For smaller, reusable content structures that are embedded within other content types (for example, a "Hero Banner" component). Components are not standalone pages.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e29fac1193a317c743275b0591a303cc0">
<code>_section</code> – An extension of <code>_component</code> that lets editors add components in a grid structure. Sections can only be used within experiences.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eead4b8d45f6e162d65256d68503c9323">
<code>_media</code> – For generic media assets.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e20cfdc6ecdd307e6728a09d019798725">
<code>_image</code> – For image assets.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee62cf9263a08e1530303187403ed0ae2">
<code>_video</code> – For video assets. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e06070465893b441bbc648f3047c3d08e">
<p><code>Properties</code> – A JSON object defining the fields (properties) of your content type. Each property has its own <code>displayName</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>localized</code> status, <code>required</code> status, <code>group</code>, <code>sortOrder</code>, and <code>indexingType</code>. The following is an example:</p>
<pre><code class="language-auto language-graphql">{
    "Title": {
        "displayName": "Title of the page",
        "type": "string",
        "localized": true,
        "required": true,
        "group": "Information",
        "sortOrder": 10,
        "indexingType": "searchable"
    }
}</code></pre>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e461bc5c264f8f7460c3c92df50c9eab1">(Optional) <code>CompositionBehaviors</code> – Applicable only to <code>_component</code> base types. Specifies where the component can be used. Valid values are <code>'sectionEnabled'</code> (usable within an experience) and <code>'elementEnabled'</code> (usable within a section).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea340339268dc754fcfab1e427f2ef3ca">(Optional) <code>MayContainTypes</code> – Applicable only to <code>_page</code> and <code>_experience</code> base types. Specifies which other content types can be placed as children beneath an instance of this content type in the site structure.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee59527b4b807cd6fbf5481467f18cb5d">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eeef69b5e80ea9da54a86e5a3cb1273c1"><em>Create a content type for "Blog Post" with fields for title, author, and content.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef83b13939a05795bbd9adf1f01befff3"><em>I need a new component content type called "CallToAction" that has a headline, description, and a link.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea624d40db282b9205cb5e16d91b5bda6"><em>Define an experience content type named "LandingPage" that can contain various components.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e28e0534295b8227e1e7972530fd8240c"><em>Create a content type for "ProductReview" that includes fields for rating, reviewer name, and review text.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_delete_content_type</code> – Performs a non-disruptive deletion of a content type in CMS (SaaS).</summary><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e8b14e3fa26d0d462801e422eb6862912"><div class="important">This tool is designed for safe deletion. If the content type is currently in use (meaning there are content instances based on it or other content types refer to it), the deletion fails to prevent data loss or broken references. </div></li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecad0422d7cc808c07acb271d61f01654"><div class="important">If you need to delete a content type that is in use, you need to delete or reassign all content instances and references before attempting to delete the content type itself.</div></li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e18ef610ca66f12714589e787b375b071">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e01fa327990655d07f58ae3300afc6df5">Remove a content type that you previously created, for example, using the <code>cms_create_content_type</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eaa1096fa8b8985d8c385503ab32803de">Clean up unused or outdated content type definitions from your CMS (SaaS) instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3347e6b998f8f17b53b10f10616f56a5">Ensure that a content type is no longer available for content creation, provided it's not in use.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e184e93408a7f5f17460298015695fe6a">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e8c31d8ecfe3c94febddc37f466fed976">
<code>ContentTypeKey</code> – The unique machine-readable key of the existing content type in CMS (SaaS) instance that you want to delete.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2275260b2df1ee7fea787a16a7d82e86">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e33fc2f197743b979f67170feeee8f00c"><em>Delete the content type with the key 'OldBlogPost'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5cdcb6ab15ce13f5446faaaf168ada2f"><em>Remove the 'TemporaryPromo' content type from my CMS (SaaS.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eef296858f070ee84d833ae59fbd86b7d"><em>Can you delete the content type named 'DraftArticle'?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_update_content_type</code> – Updates an existing content type in CMS (SaaS) using a <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7386" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">JSON Merge Patch</a> algorithm.</summary><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e13ec2516ab030de049b6c5c192942098">
<strong>Non-disruptive updates</strong> – The <code>cms_update_content_type</code> tool prioritizes the integrity of your existing content. If an update would cause a <code>BreakingChanges</code> error (for example, changing a field's type in a way that would invalidate existing content), the operation fails. In such cases, if the content type was initially created by you, you might need to consider deleting it (if it has no content instances) and recreating it with the desired properties.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea14da645334c5e3af6da248747ab0c67">
<strong>Property groups</strong> – Any <code>group</code> you specify for a property must reference an existing property group. You can use the <code>cms_list_property_groups</code> tool to see available groups or <code>cms_create_property_group</code> tool to create one. See the <a href="#h_01K8XJ5H66WA32H2T126Y5YJ7Y">Property groups</a> section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1ee4e6d2b2bd1b1c589270640c6693d0">
<strong>Partial updates</strong> – You only need to provide the properties you intend to update. Any properties not included in your request remain unchanged.</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea20045e5b22ea813b56be707c9ffa4a7">
<div class="important"><strong>When to use</strong></div>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e2a2a322e90726d62c04035f58383b9b7">Modify specific properties of an existing content type (for example, change the <code>displayName</code> of a field, update its <code>description</code>, or adjust its <code>maxLength</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed70dc0827c41498c773b77f2699af11d">Add new properties to an existing content type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7315dbe09b9896ccb473fc886679003c">Update the <code>baseType</code>, <code>CompositionBehaviors</code>, <code>Description</code>, <code>DisplayName</code>, or <code>MayContainTypes</code> of a content type, provided the changes are non-disruptive.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eb4b1520ac93164a2848c05b2c2d6e55d">
<div class="important"><strong>Properties</strong></div>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e5a2ab135edf65efeb45fb0134a80fa8c">
<code>Key</code> – The machine-readable key of the content type you want to update.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e40e6db0edee29d85c71c80c653c4eef2">(Optional) <code>DisplayName</code> – The new human-readable name for the content type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efacca605a0a18105f6013e434d73034e">(Optional) <code>Description</code> – The new description for the content type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7f99227b47dfb19bf4d1b9aa97dd645e">(Optional) <code>BaseType</code> – The new base type for the content type. Valid values include the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e06da8fdcaf3594e5b74319dfa7a34aed"> <code>_page</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee9e3a6eb14b9ee430fad29191ab3fe73"><code>_experience</code></li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed6b097a738b9c454107ec3a181aa2433"><code>_component</code></li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb6c593e1bbc77fac0116df5c70a28bae">
<code>_section</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3597f5038a44b50a3b7cebc02a7a496a"><code>_media</code></li>
<li data-list-item-id="ece4263999e8b10af41f9c7627ddede0e"><code>_image</code></li>
<li data-list-item-id="e760b6580dd7ef0eb12cca714a15ef708"><code>_video</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1a8750a5a6a086b483067c10fc1285a5">
<p>(Optional) <code>Properties</code> – A JSON object containing the properties you want to update or add. For example, the following JSON changes the display name of an existing 'Title' property:</p>
<pre class="language-json">{
    "Title": {
        "displayName": "Title of the page"
    }</pre>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><h2 id="h_01K5W7KQH9AZFNNDSP00KNA0DG">Content items<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K5W7KQH9AZFNNDSP00KNA0DG"></a></h2><details><summary><code>cms_create_content_item</code> – Creates a new empty content instance in CMS (SaaS) based on an existing content type.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e8f947e51d77b32698493803ac3e072a9">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e3eff9dff9bf1893ffdbe584cab3fbda4">When you need to create a new content item in the CMS.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e63e086e0d0fa9ed439bc0241b1ee7724">To create an empty draft content item before populating its properties.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2fc4a1a22ed4b76fcb72389c90884234">To create pages or experiences under other page or experience containers.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1cc57e2743122c3e174d3ded0bb5e985">To create shared or standalone components within a folder container. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea0b8403b5b783ad56c1e0f2d63ec2579">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea6a9b3c62cffa6d0d73f9b3fa8f3f3d4">
<code>Locale</code> – The locale or language code for this content instance. For example, 'en' or 'en-US'.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5f2134b752875fa170e4f8c7c33d9f81">
<code>ContentType</code> – The key of the existing content type to create an instance of.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7f4d5e4bbf747adba49eff50e066dda4">
<code>DisplayName</code> – The display name of the content instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef2f30e770b7449bb80d4944a53506804">(Optional) <code>Container</code> – The key of the parent content item to create the item in.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1e3d71562f531cb09cd7acbed11dfdfd">(Optional) <code>Owner</code> – The key of the owner content.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e951283e4e158670918cce14a65261e78">(Optional) <code>RouteSegment</code> – URL segment for routing to this content (for pages and experiences).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec7301e9ec9b18915eb157f65f052aa69">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8557fee1e60ab39ef13ef18f9172b856"><em>Create a new 'Article' content item named 'My First Article' in English.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e965af384e1aad61f6825f90fd95a2d41"><em>I want to create a new page called 'About Us' with the content type 'StandardPage' for the 'en-US' locale.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e89d72323facf3e2402f8ea31d28426f7"><em>Make a new component of type 'HeroBlock' named 'Homepage Hero' in the shared asset folder.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_create_content_variation</code> – Creates a content variation (alternative version) for an existing page or experience content item.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e80ba85b00434b002f53b2c5af03f3247">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e1f0bad98700933f0ee5a7995160dcd47">When you want to create an alternative version of a page or experience for A/B testing or experimentation.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee0634621edd71ecf571d3ef7dec36799">To deliver audience-specific content by creating targeted variations of existing pages or experiences.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e245a7960179cb896dcdcc80aab3a9b08">To create a new variation that starts empty (inheriting from the default version) or copies properties from an existing variation.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7552a0290774f6785b33a1844e381277">After creating the variation, use the <code>cms_update_content_item</code> tool o set the properties that should differ from the default version.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e02f2209aa142aee5642901c9e4b5e94c">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb01e689b22fd5e9dadf21d615853ff22">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The unique identifier of the content item to create a variation for. Must be a page or experience content type (not a component). Accepts GUID format with or without hyphens.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e303b0886c8a5c036db108e2f50aad9c0">
<code>Variation</code> – The unique key identifier for this variation. Must start with a letter and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores (2–50 characters). For example, 'VariantA', 'Holiday2024', 'ExperimentB_Control'.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e698a890b0514d5abf9bb3e136ef96973">(Optional) <code>DisplayName</code> – The display name for this variation as shown to editors. If not provided, a name is auto-generated based on the variation key.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e63391111cc70b4e7bd3c7b1d1b0c3d7f">(Optional) <code>CopyFromVariation</code> – The variation key to copy properties from when creating this new variation. If not specified, the new variation starts empty, inheriting from the default version.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8cddbe5dc4194b4ba60b2c843dce377e">(Optional) <code>Locale</code> – The locale or language code for the variation content. For example, 'en', 'sv', or 'en-US'. If not specified, the content's default locale is used.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2e12a5475a0cdf5cd6a943be7f3abf29">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e55d67dcb24fcfd0ea84b987e0302fb19"><em>Create a variation called 'VariantA' for the homepage content item 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e47989e460397c407f1b2da3fc90948c6"><em>I want to create a holiday variation of my landing page, copying the properties from the existing 'VariantA' variation.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e507ec7f03ab9d08e320b8faa42a03e07"><em>Make a new variation named 'ExperimentB_Control' for page 'abc123def456' in English.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_get_content_data</code> – Retrieves CMS (SaaS) content data for a specific content item.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee8fc7d976ae45577247fb802af0ca252">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e7263fc6481dd578f854ebdf957a75118">To retrieve the content and metadata of a specific content item.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e794bfdb3d5efc1007cee7de26ac917bc">To verify the existence and details of a content item before performing other operations like deletion or update.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebaf5f171be029a02dbf352a40374ea84">To get the published version of a content item by default.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec433bd3c50cd9b4022ce973ecd3cb1a3">To retrieve a specific version of a content item if a version number is provided.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="efa84a8de06cc3f0ac81cc0840ad13f58">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e34bc924a1c2b5dfdafa5b9d40d3acbaa">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The unique identifier for the content item to retrieve.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee4ba25b98904d21fa36e18a73ace59c3">(Optional) <code>ContentVersion</code> – The specific version number of the content to retrieve.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e74fd654c9576993bf2e271e1549622d4">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8803f76d7a4f5322da7d1f84b18d1e1e"><em>Get the content data for content item 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="edebfc6880881fe08a7bd8990eb1387a5"><em>Show me the details of the article with key 'abc123def456'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e3714186366790de168e6aaa7d3db42aa"><em>Retrieve version 3 of the content item 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5'.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_get_content_preview_url</code> – Generates a preview URL with authentication tokens for viewing draft or published content in configured preview applications.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e38f9409774897a537ab769fe7f73f1d9">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef838acdcc49e3f89878466c461c7b755">When you need to preview a specific version of a content item before publishing.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2fc8b27a6bc7cf877ed1f1029b1524e3">To share an authenticated preview link with content editors or stakeholders.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edec779425c237f37a18db7e4ea4f8af1">To verify how draft content renders across one or more configured preview applications.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e59e0ad7e254f2427a3d2acd44b264af0">To review a previously published version of a content item.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eefa56e189c9c14045946df50df8a6cbd">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e746a90abc6733202e8bd899cc5857fd3">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The unique identifier of the content item. Accepts GUID format with or without hyphens. For example, 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5' or 'c3558e0800a645d0bfff5bd2bda3acb5'.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea2077af60640df8be9a157a1c69714c1">
<code>ContentVersion</code> – The version number of the content to preview. For example, 1, 2, or 3. Each version represents a distinct state of the content item.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e19829457a8aab25fe46f85f20fa03957">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e70ee555fd6921c0d73711237ef2b8829"><em>Show me a preview of version 3 of the content item with key 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec7d13954033bc274880ce816b688fed1"><em>Generate a preview URL for the draft I just updated.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eef5c8d50f5a2354735593a5e3cf8d6fd"><em>I want to share a preview link for version 2 of my homepage content.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_delete_content_item</code> – Deletes a content item from CMS (SaaS) using its unique content key.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee64bb0b12433d42e8524e607e56936be">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e3417ba7429ef60a891f2ac6451d212bc">When you need to remove a specific content item from CMS (SaaS).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5b4bab2001735005375be06aa741358a">After verifying the content key using <code>cms_get_content_data</code> to ensure the correct item is targeted for deletion.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebbf79a4f6fa48eaa85bb23e5380f019c">When a content item is no longer needed or is outdated.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e30e6fd1e1a7972b94e66806229f14989">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="ee6b636651c59adff637b2f8dff078e68">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The unique identifier for the content item to delete.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e63803a3127a3462bb2183710e4fd704a">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e3fbde9ae60451defd4adedc833e54a6a"><em>Delete the content item with key 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e4dce60d68bdc059d790350ea95e31c9d"><em>Remove the old blog post.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e15420b1825b9af078fa6393cf27cc385"><em>I want to delete content item 'abc123def456'.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_publish_content_item</code> – Publishes a specific content version in CMS (SaaS), making it visible to site visitors.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1db5ee3db5fb5c4975991b1bb6e3c965">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e898c0b6cf48cf41b58ec04c47a216004">To make a specific version of a content item live and visible to site visitors.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb58b3326e41381ffe07f1edfb018a33f">To immediately publish content or schedule it for a future date and time.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5a40cbfa8f2f491915225fac35eb18cc">When a content item has been reviewed and is ready for public release.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e923feb481e622402ea2fca3678deb72b">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eebc43c570f27c4457ca219a157421596">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The key of the content item to publish.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9ce4d292bfcd10bfa5de3f29a0984022">
<code>ContentVersion</code> – The version number of the content to publish.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eaafbd5375926d5bb14d2a64f11f589ab">(Optional) <code>DelayPublishUntil</code> – Optional scheduled publish date and time in ISO 8601 format.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ef97de28644e5f3f3470980e7a4e821ed">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e2747c973cb8750ad1381aede70c8bc7a"><em>Publish content item 'abc123def456' version 5.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e10a3f1f2bba359b862061b913a9583c9"><em>Schedule content 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5' version 2 to publish on 2026-02-01 at 10 AM UTC.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e2196f34ca80b64094fb3ef248147625f"><em>Make version 7 of the 'Homepage' content item live now.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_update_content_item</code> – Updates the value for any property of a content item using a "JSON Merge Patch" algorithm.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed75e8f9d46c0cbef32f92dbef9315a43">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e9aa33e3b505c0ca2c5463ae0e79ba98f">To modify existing properties of a content item.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6c9857b1a3a3d34b91436be5bcfe41d4">To create a new draft version or update an existing draft.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e636e6edd23182c3721ac079d7fed62f3">To update specific fields without affecting other properties.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9c444bfd036baaacfaf16f2d7a98a0a4">To clear or remove property values. For example, setting an array to <code>[]</code> or a property to <code>null</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec7721dc16a8b4d84beaf65a0af0e30e8">To update complex properties like content references, link URLs, content areas, or rich text.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e480f47c8acf50644367f2b01b5dfb155">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e54eaa46c8c06df45d8ff23c0284e1404">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The unique identifier for the content instance in CMS (SaaS).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef9fe8b4ee0e949317e4e09f9e6653e97">
<code>Properties</code> – A JSON object containing the property names and their new values.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea3f5c2e48ac6f046c5439890458322db">(Optional) <code>ContentVersion</code> – The specific version number to update.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea3564dbb83028c0df3a7b1ea8850cc6b">(Optional) <code>Locale</code> – The locale and language code for the content item.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e815721df289e83136caaf952a7115555">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e22ee13d8f89ace8e31cbe84374eb7003"><em>Update the title of content item 'abc123def456' to 'New Product Launch'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e85c81ec2baf4b82489b77d6f18de9ea3"><em>Change the description of content 'c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5' in English to 'An exciting new feature'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea0757a54ebeeac22e7aaadb12cd6d21b"><em>Set the 'HeroImage' of content 'xyz789' to 'cms://content/image_guid'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e6988b74c8ce8b8f17cabd38547aba126"><em>Clear the 'Tags' list for content item 'tag_item_key'.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><h2 id="h_01KG0129WW92R9YK10FW5C3T0W">Get content<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KG0129WW92R9YK10FW5C3T0W"></a></h2><details><summary><code>cms_get_content_data</code> – Get the data from a specific content instance in CMS (SaaS).</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e7abd4f1131e72c48aa96218e09cce38b">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e971b896f1bbc6767b67de83cfcc59f80">Retrieve the content of a specific item from your CMS (SaaS) instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6bbdee430fff3ecf6f2d05a1fca97f95">Access a particular version of a content item, for example, to compare changes or revert to an older state.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e34d64e337352aed8a37c7c9d1b79fa22">Get the published version of a content item to display or analyze.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee287aa5ed710eb2dd906b5cdb37305fb">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e47646f167faa0c760fc6f25ebe9e9b96">
<code>ContentKey</code> – The key of the content item you want to retrieve. This is the unique identifier for the content instance in CMS (SaaS), typically formatted as a GUID (with or without hyphens). For example, <code>c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5</code> or <code>c3558e0800a645d0bfff5bd2bda3acb5</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e86c601397837ff93ebd4361afcac49f2">(Optional) <code>ContentVersion</code> – The specific version number of the content key you want to retrieve. You should include this parameter only when you explicitly provide a version number. Otherwise, omit it to get the published versions.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eeea21a039feba6ab1a896ddc54ada842">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec0544637545884af7d0c43e22d2cfec2">
<em>Get the content data for the article with key </em><code><em>c3558e08-00a6-45d0-bfff-5bd2bda3acb5</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed3ac4f27ba6c82ce6fb28cb2a3d0c648"><em>Show me the content of the 'Homepage' page.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1a2c2bbfc7a2e30e534f994f9706516d">
<em>Retrieve version 3 of the content with key </em><code><em>12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e86a0985f199fb1cbe35f345c57454fea"><em>What is the published content for the 'AboutUsPage'?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><h2 id="h_01K5F02YMXT7CH8AKMKXNVTGQM">Styles<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K5F02YMXT7CH8AKMKXNVTGQM"></a></h2><p><a href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/update/docs/work-with-styles" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Styles</a> (also called display templates) control how content is rendered in the Visual Builder. Each style (template) is associated with exactly one type: a composition node type (for example, section, row, or column), a content base type (for example, page or component), or a specific content type key.</p><details><summary><code>cms_list_display_templates</code> – Lists all styles (display templates) registered in the CMS, including their type association, default state, and a summary of their settings.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee969cfbcf08d1fbb7a1084f1b7ddab18">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ede32dc329aeafe13c36069b7a00cc3ed">Get an overview of all styles currently configured in your CMS instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5374f1eef93d86b4b060d08468d61ca5">Check which styles are set as the default for a given content type or layout node.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebbc77a871061ca46116a078dcc404748">Review the settings available on each style before creating or updating one.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e386b73c8a946ee37508377d0988446e8">Identify the key for a specific style to use with <code>cms_get_display_template</code> or <code>cms_update_display_template</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebaca097d3787ba7817cf46726e29208f">
<strong>Parameters</strong><br>This tool has no parameters.</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eaf7aee2fc382f7e20e0fae85e0f730c2">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0d0f8f3cb82fe72ca93a439fd3e3139c"><em>List all styles in my CMS instance.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e43fca757c687d4ff55e15136e9b87387"><em>Show me all available styles and their settings.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e91d42723ee49c4d5fb7efc4723587ac9"><em>Which styles are set as default in my CMS?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_get_display_template</code> – Gets the full details of a style (display template) by its key, including all settings and choices.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee9f391162f6073f14bcc343b77fc9b14">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e47aa2c8871df52a7d8143b5c3409f7fa">Inspect the full configuration of a specific style, including all its settings and available choices.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5ef93f19dd0d0ee5f2728b127619b1d3">Verify the settings on a style before updating it.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e424e02b7781cba0ee5598bdd494776bc">Retrieve the exact setting names and choice values needed to reference when creating a similar style.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed8ce8443337ab1d8e10b2c8aed01af63">Confirm whether a style is set as the default for its associated content type or node type.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e67f20218634b3db3bb7d664fa8403f4c">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e97c539fe71df82b9fc895a2319f255f4">
<code>Key</code> – The unique key identifying the style to retrieve.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea498b44f8da42fd07e1094be67aaad6e">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5c05c04a4ff1afbb014fdc104da9db79"><em>Show me the full details for the style with the key "HeroImageLeft".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efd231b8719598b0e890bcf7250148734"><em>What settings and choices does the "CardTeaser" style have?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0c9d98cdfffe1b357cb6c7339f9d62e7"><em>Get the style details for "DefaultSection".</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_create_display_template</code> – Creates a new style (display template) in CMS.  A style (display template) must be associated with exactly one of the following: a layout node type (for example, section, row, or column), a content base type (for example, page or component), or a specific content type.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e67ad8c126fd4031fe12b292549a60c99">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea0b6843851690f425afdf119ba8580af">Create a new style for a specific content type, such as a hero block or article page.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea8d7c188f88f992eb28ad913ea5c262e">Add a default style for a layout node type, such as a section or row.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2e15f53efbfb37d9ef8e8ebd05425ac1">Define a style with specific settings and choices, such as background color or image position, for editors to select in Visual Builder.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e94a151a955ad12e83a393986deb116d6">Create a style that applies to all content of a given base type, such as all components or all pages.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee559ac7471985fb044ad45a9b36ff0b5">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="edf8b2dcab3b75772cba4dae3018d2014">
<code>DisplayName</code> – The human-readable name of the style shown in the UI, for example, <em>Wide Hero</em> or <em>Default Section</em>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2acfea14ee50a5a193afe0e5fe46df68">(Optional) <code>Key</code> – Optional unique identifier for the style. If omitted, a key will be auto-generated by the server. Example: <code>HeroBlockWide</code>, <code>DefaultSection</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e336de4b7b0727a3c89b2c760c937d7ed">(Optional) <code>NodeType</code> – For layout node types. Valid values include: <code>section</code>, <code>row</code>, <code>column</code>. Only one of nodeType, baseType, or contentType should be provided.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2756a6af53515d060568e3a777b618e8">(Optional) <code>BaseType</code> – For content base types. Valid values: <code>_page</code>, <code>_component</code>, <code>_media</code>, <code>_image</code>, <code>_video</code>, <code>_folder</code>, <code>_experience</code>, <code>_section</code>, <code>_element</code>. Only one of nodeType, baseType, or contentType should be provided.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64ad265efe17c6ca54330d1f69998891">(Optional) <code>ContentType</code> – For specific content types, for example, <code>HeroBlock</code>, <code>ArticlePage</code>. Only one of nodeType, baseType, or contentType should be provided.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e267ec5c5cbd5d6a8edb2f9bd45d42381">(Optional) <code>IsDefault</code> – Whether this style is the default for its associated type. Defaults to false.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e428beb4063e4ba389061d036555ff9c2">(Optional) <code>Settings</code> – Settings for the style as a JSON object. Each setting can have choices that users can select from. Setting fields: <code>displayName</code> (required), <code>editor</code> (optional), <code>sortOrder</code> (optional), <code>choices</code> (optional dictionary of <code>{ displayName, sortOrder }</code>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e54c79c84c3cb6f1b338fd068cd3c82a9">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e163c0f47e7516bb6a09d19f4794e4b5d"><em>Create a style called "Wide Hero" for the HeroBlock content type with a background color setting that has light and dark choices.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e07426a8cdbe1859f4094af36b6fac6c9"><em>Add a default style for the section node type called "Default Section".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea7c316a11eae27872bb1c84b6a4a8545"><em>Create a new style for all components called "Rounded Corners" with the key "ComponentRounded".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecc3eecd6d82bcd646957745febac43aa"><em>Set up a style for ArticlePage with an image position setting that lets editors choose between left and right.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>cms_update_display_template</code> – Updates an existing style (display template) in CMS. Only the provided fields are updated; all other fields remain unchanged. When settings are provided, they replace all existing settings entirely. Any existing settings not included in the update will be removed. Include all desired settings in a single call.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ede818eec0273a336375e5d2c1cfda996">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6c494085d59ddff21452e426ec942641">Rename an existing style without changing its settings or type association.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec3f63dea2b04957dca769c1a2ce71584">Set a style as the default for its associated content type or node type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edd0540972d8254e90b3d8835bff97394">Update or replace the settings and choices on an existing style.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edd46beac3b878fceb25cd204d21019a8">Change the content type or node type a style is associated with.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec2e5ae15ac37d020f3efed9d8cfd9ed3">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb449057421f30ff6dd34375bb08741d5">
<code>Key</code> – The unique key of the style to update. Example: <code>HeroBlockWide</code>, <code>DefaultSection</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edc97748baa18ed3d40fe913e7ffc98ed">(Optional) <code>DisplayName</code> – The human-readable name of the style shown in the UI, for example, <code>Wide Hero</code> or <code>Default Section</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e748f5c9df8332bf4e0cedcb83e7fe520">(Optional) <code>NodeType</code> – For layout node types. Valid values include: <code>section</code>, <code>row</code>, <code>column</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e16e188bfdc41ddd60539e357dcbf07a4">(Optional) <code>BaseType</code> – For content base types. Valid values: <code>_page</code>, <code>_component</code>, <code>_media</code>, <code>_image</code>, <code>_video</code>, <code>_folder</code>, <code>_experience</code>, <code>_section</code>, <code>_element</code>'.</li>

</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e14a5fabd978190107ea91dfd876ddc58">

</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>get_idealab_domain_keywords</code> – Returns Idea Lab domain organic competition data.</summary><div><ul>

</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>get_idealab_keyword_infos</code> – Returns Idea Lab SEO keyword information.</summary><div><ul>

</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>get_idealab_keyword_keyword_questions</code> – Returns common questions for an Idea Lab SEO keyword in a given country. This is highly valuable for content creation, FAQ development, and understanding user intent.</summary><div><ul>

</ul>
</li>

<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e3b26f5927259a9b8232646da6512284f">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e58f733948649299411eea74bbcdc57df">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">keyword</code> – The main keyword for which you want to find related terms.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e02bb8f7ed453bd31c6a567a996164fb8">
<code data-axiom="1.7.1">country_code</code> – The two-letter ISO country code (for example., 'us', 'de', and 'au') for the analysis.</li>

<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e4adf06fb16101e592b1db65e2efec1aa">

</li>
</ul></div></details><h2 id="h_01KG7YGAGGQ87SR099NPTRB9E2">Optimizely Graph tools<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KG7YGAGGQ87SR099NPTRB9E2"></a></h2><div class="note">The Optimizely Graph tools are available for CMS (SaaS) and CMS 12 for users who also have Optimizely Graph.</div><details><summary><code>graph_content_type_schema</code> – Use as your starting point for understanding the content structure within your Optimizely Graph instance. The tool lets you and Opal discover available content types and their fields, which is crucial for constructing accurate GraphQL queries.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e35fc97e085dcc92b724dd9837c961166">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e79aae07303535be4a3c48aaa75d7942d">
<strong>To explore available content</strong> – If you want to know what types of content (for example, articles, products, pages) are stored in your Optimizely Graph instance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2d278e035d3d40dbdbac0e3705ebe8ae">
<strong>To understand content structure</strong> – If you need to see the fields and properties associated with a specific content type before querying it.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4c3696c6b12d24b4bdee8f512f9c2061">
<strong>To build GraphQL queries</strong> – If you need the exact content type names and field names for use with the <code>graph_content_graphql_executor</code> tool.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e3d8fc67814fb72abae53494fd7540dc8">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea2e08fc777ca336fa6f132b244114ca9">(Optional) <code>searchPhrase</code> – A text string to filter content types that are relevant to your question, for example, "news article" or "product details". If left empty, all content types are returned.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1d4253f48187a5815118b1f7377dc2b7">(Optional) <code>itemMinimumScore</code> – The minimum score for items to be considered relevant based on the search phrase.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e81fd6d0fe50267de024ac8421721e63a">(Optional) <code>contentTypeFacetLimit</code> – The maximum number of content types to return from the facet.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="edf9b2f1e677490c524edada2dac8abbf">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5555b748918e663c60cedfb7967d8802"><em>What content types are available in Optimizely Graph?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef8aa31bec13df7378114ae66803317e5"><em>Show me the schema for content types related to 'blog posts'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb9d7964414cc4b107c5a0745532222eb"><em>I want to see all content types and their fields that are relevant to 'products'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e00c388d7f4a5da822f9acbdb470a1078"><em>Can you list content types that might contain information about 'customer reviews'?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>graph_content_graphql_executor</code> – Execute custom GraphQL queries against your Optimizely Graph instance. You can retrieve specific content items, filter results, sort, and get aggregated data (facets).</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e275b465ed1401de5dbce591373977097">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb134a3fc68a4619feb66d2123d027713">
<strong>To retrieve specific content items</strong> – If you need to fetch detailed data for articles, products, pages, or any other content type.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e77dc476c8951163823ac7affd9f81bc1">
<strong>To filter content based on criteria</strong> – If you want to find content that matches certain conditions, for example, articles published within a date range or products with a specific tag.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb2773584f522fe128edf4877a2f4bc29">
<strong>To sort content results</strong> – If you need to order content by fields like publication date, title, or price.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e544d7fed9037dabe82daa30b28837310">
<strong>To paginate through large datasets</strong> – If you need to retrieve content in chunks using <code>skip</code> and <code>limit</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eda23a687c61d1861a264704e2cf02020">
<strong>To get aggregated data (facets)</strong> – If you want to count occurrences of values within a field, for example, the number of articles per author or products per category.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee1c4fd9aa504b00bf4e91749f1c49c08">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eee22966bf3033638ad4227d357a4db4d">
<code>query</code> – The GraphQL query to execute.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e222b1d25be33096b63d114fb6b5eeab3">(Optional) <code>variablesAsJson</code> – A JSON string representing variables for the GraphQL query.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e429f50a645c397e5839a4db619ee3a38">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e30d954c47b7f9d04c88c1968f62eee41"><em>Get the titles and descriptions of all 'NewsArticle' content types.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e080fbbcf976d0ac856a488ddd216dd58"><em>Find all 'Product' content types where the 'price' is greater than 50 and less than 100, and order them by price in ascending order. Also, show me the 'name' and 'sku' of these products. </em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb1d31c6113cca2a70a7bdaf69b25be43"><em>Count how many 'BlogPosts' were published each month in 2024, and list their titles.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>graph_content_search_tool</code> – Use as a simpler alternative for searching content in Optimizely Graph when constructing complex GraphQL queries might be excessive. It lets you search for content based on a search phrase across a specified content type.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e7c249c4f816ca7a6f385a36378a34450">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul data-axiom="1.7.1">
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="ee916d1f9c8146d04b108d76af498fb08">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">For simple keyword searches</strong> – If you need to find content items that contain a specific phrase or keyword.</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e8ecc134687fe2fffced52b7958267ce8">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">When you know the content type</strong> – If you are looking for content within a known content type, for example, <em>Search for 'summer sale' in 'Promotions'.</em>
</li>
<li data-axiom="1.7.1" data-list-item-id="e267f957ab88d1f218c9e2fe33207d07d">
<strong data-axiom="1.7.1">As a quick lookup</strong> – If the <code data-axiom="1.7.1">graph_content_graphql_executor</code> tool seems too complex or overextravagant for your immediate need.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ebc26e5beddfa0faeb1de987d1b9c5da2">
<strong>Parameters:</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e594644a5343db78093b92fd75ccc5e38">
<code>searchPhrase</code> – The search phrase to use when searching for content.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebbb0cab8ef560b137c540a30cbd699d0">(Optional) <code>contentTypeName</code> – The specific content type to search within, for example, "Article" or "Product". If not provided, it defaults to "Data" (which might search across various types depending on configuration).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5a7eca062d9a35c4955e3448da0364ef">
<p>(Optional) <code>outputFieldsAsGraphQLOutput</code> – The specific fields you want to retrieve for the matching content items, in GraphQL output format. If not provided, it defaults to <code>_fulltext</code>. For example, the following:</p>
<pre class="language-auto">"id name createdBy { id name }"</pre>
</li>

            <a class="flex-1 py-2 text-inherit font-semibold" :class="{ 'text-inherit': !isOpen }" href="<%= section.html_url %>">
              <%= section.name %>
            </a>
            <button class="p-2 ml-1 not-a-button border-radius transition cursor-pointer hover:bg-gray-200" :class="{ 'is-active': isOpen }" :aria-expanded="isOpen" data-toggle="collapse" data-target="#section-<%= section.id %>">

                <path d="M162,190 C156,190 150,187 146,183 L7,38 C-2,29 -2,15 7,7 C16,-2 30,-2 39,7 L162,135 L285,7 C293,-2 308,-2 317,7 C326,15 326,29 317,38 L178,183 C174,187 168,190 162,190 Z"></path>
              </svg>
            </button>
          </div>

          
          <%= partial('partial-article-list-sections', {
            id: 'section-' + section.id,
            parentId: '#' + id,
            sections: section.sections,
            activeCategoryId: activeCategoryId,
            activeSectionId: activeSectionId,
            activeArticleId: activeArticleId,
            partial: partial
          }) %>

          
          <% if (section.articles.length) { %>
            <ul class="list-none font-size-md pl-0 mb-0 collapse" :class="{ 'is-visible': isOpen }" id="section-<%= section.id %>" data-parent="#<%= id %>">

                  <a class="block px-3 py-2 text-inherit border-radius transition<% if (article.isActive) { %> bg-gray-100<% } %>" href="<%= article.html_url %>">
                    <%= article.title %>
                  </a>
                </li>

            </ul>
          <% } %>

        </li>
      <% }); %>
    </ul>
  <% } %>

BodyMarkdown:
System tools for Content Management System (SaaS) – Support Help Center                   

[Skip to main content](#page-container)

System tools are built-in features that help Optimizely Opal take action. Each tool performs a specific task, such as creating a campaign, uploading files, or generating images. Think of tools like attachments on a Swiss Army knife. Each one has a distinct purpose that helps you get work done.

In addition to the [system tools available in Opal](/hc/en-us/articles/39340107628429), Optimizely Content Management System (CMS) (SaaS) includes a set of system tools to help you with CMS-related tasks, such as managing content.

Ask Opal what tools it has at any time. For example, enter _"Please list the tools you have with a brief description of what they do and the parameters"_ into [Opal Chat](/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813).

Click a tool's name to expand it and learn when to use it, its required and optional parameters, and example prompts for calling the tool. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.

## Content types[](#h_01K5W6R30FHS5TSMTC84131WBX)

[Content types](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/content-types-saas#/) act as blueprints for your content, specifying what kind of data each piece of content can hold. For example, a "News Article" content type might have fields for title, body, author, and publish date.

`cms_list_content_types` – Gets a list of content types, excluding properties, from CMS (SaaS). This tool provides an overview of the available content structures you can use, without providing the full details of each property.

*   **When to use**
    *   See all the content types that are available in your CMS (SaaS) instance.
    *   Understand the different kinds of content you can create or manage.
    *   Identify content types before performing actions like creating new content, getting detailed information about a specific content type (using `cms_get_content_type_details`), or creating a new content type (using `cms_create_content_type`).
    *   Filter content types by their base type (for example, to see only pages or only components).
*   **Properties**
    *   (Optional) `BaseType` – Filter the list of content types by their base type. If you do not provide a  `BaseType`, the tool returns all content types. Valid values include the following: 
        *   `_page` 
        *   `_experience`
        *    `_component`
        *    `_media`
        *    `_image`
        *    `_video`
        *    `_section`
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all content types in my CMS (SaaS) instance._
    *   _What content types are available?_
    *   _Show me all the page content types._
    *   _Can you list all the component content types?_
    *   _What media content types do we have?_

`cms_get_content_type_details` – Gets the full details of a content type, including properties, from CMS (SaaS).

*   **When to use**
    *   Inspect the complete structure and configuration of an existing content type.
    *   Understand all the fields (properties) defined for a content type, their types, and other settings.
    *   Get detailed information about a content type after listing them with the `cms_list_content_types` tool.
    *   Review a content type's definition before making updates with `cms_update_content_type` or creating new content based on it.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `ContentTypeKey` – The unique machine-readable key for an existing content type in your CMS (SaaS) instance.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Get the full details for the 'Article' content type._
    *   _Show me all the properties of the content type with the key 'ProductPage'._
    *   _Can you provide the complete schema for the 'HeroComponent' content type?_

`cms_create_content_type` – Creates a new content type in CMS (SaaS).

*   New content types must follow the same conventions (for example, naming conventions) as existing content types. Use the `cms_list_content_types` tool to get existing content types and the `cms_get_content_type_details` tool to get details, including all properties for a specific content type.
*   If you are creating multiple content types, always create and register content types with `baseType: "_component"` first. This ensures that other content types can properly reference them.
*   The `group` field for a property must reference an existing property group. Use the `cms_list_property_groups` tool to list existing property groups or the `cms_create_property_group` tool to create one. See the [Property groups](#h_01K8XJ5H66WA32H2T126Y5YJ7Y) section.

*   **When to use**
    *   Define a new structure for a specific type of content you want to manage in your CMS (SaaS) instance.
    *   Create content models for pages, experiences, components, or sections.
    *   Standardize the properties and behaviors of content items across your website or application.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `Key` – A machine-readable key that must be unique in your instance of CMS (SaaS) (for example, 'NewsArticle', 'HeroComponent').
    *   `DisplayName` – The human-readable name of the content type (for example, 'News Article', 'Hero').
    *   `Description` – A brief explanation of the content type's purpose (for example, 'Used to display news articles on a website').
    *   `BaseType` – The base type of the content type. Valid values include the following:
        *   `_page` – For content that has a fixed position in your site structure and a specific URL (e.g., an "About Us" page).
        *   `_experience` – Similar to `_page`, but includes a dynamic area where editors can add components and sections.
        *   `_component` – For smaller, reusable content structures that are embedded within other content types (for example, a "Hero Banner" component). Components are not standalone pages.
        *   `_section` – An extension of `_component` that lets editors add components in a grid structure. Sections can only be used within experiences.
        *   `_media` – For generic media assets.
        *   `_image` – For image assets.
        *   `_video` – For video assets. 
    *   `Properties` – A JSON object defining the fields (properties) of your content type. Each property has its own `displayName`, `type`, `localized` status, `required` status, `group`, `sortOrder`, and `indexingType`. The following is an example:
        
            {
                "Title": {
                    "displayName": "Title of the page",
                    "type": "string",
                    "localized": true,
                    "required": true,
                    "group": "Information",
                    "sortOrder": 10,
                    "indexingType": "searchable"
                }
            }

`cms_update_content_type` – Updates an existing content type in CMS (SaaS) using a [JSON Merge Patch](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7386) algorithm.

*   **Non-disruptive updates** – The `cms_update_content_type` tool prioritizes the integrity of your existing content. If an update would cause a `BreakingChanges` error (for example, changing a field's type in a way that would invalidate existing content), the operation fails. In such cases, if the content type was initially created by you, you might need to consider deleting it (if it has no content instances) and recreating it with the desired properties.
*   **Property groups** – Any `group` you specify for a property must reference an existing property group. You can use the `cms_list_property_groups` tool to see available groups or `cms_create_property_group` tool to create one. See the [Property groups](#h_01K8XJ5H66WA32H2T126Y5YJ7Y) section.
*   **Partial updates** – You only need to provide the properties you intend to update. Any properties not included in your request remain unchanged.
*   **When to use**

*   **Properties**
    
    *   `Key` – The machine-readable key of the content type you want to update.
    *   (Optional) `DisplayName` – The new human-readable name for the content type.
    *   (Optional) `Description` – The new description for the content type.
    *   (Optional) `BaseType` – The new base type for the content type. Valid values include the following:
        *    `_page`
        *   `_experience`
        *   `_component`
        *   `_section`.
        *   `_media`
        *   `_image`
        *   `_video`
    *   (Optional) `Properties` – A JSON object containing the properties you want to update or add. For example, the following JSON changes the display name of an existing 'Title' property:
        
        {
            "Title": {
                "displayName": "Title of the page"
            }

## Styles[](#h_01K5F02YMXT7CH8AKMKXNVTGQM)

[Styles](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/update/docs/work-with-styles) (also called display templates) control how content is rendered in the Visual Builder. Each style (template) is associated with exactly one type: a composition node type (for example, section, row, or column), a content base type (for example, page or component), or a specific content type key.

`cms_list_display_templates` – Lists all styles (display templates) registered in the CMS, including their type association, default state, and a summary of their settings.

*   **When to use**
    *   Get an overview of all styles currently configured in your CMS instance.
    *   Check which styles are set as the default for a given content type or layout node.
    *   Review the settings available on each style before creating or updating one.
    *   Identify the key for a specific style to use with `cms_get_display_template` or `cms_update_display_template`.
*   **Parameters**  
    This tool has no parameters.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all styles in my CMS instance._
    *   _Show me all available styles and their settings._
    *   _Which styles are set as default in my CMS?_

`cms_get_display_template` – Gets the full details of a style (display template) by its key, including all settings and choices.

*   **When to use**
    *   Inspect the full configuration of a specific style, including all its settings and available choices.
    *   Verify the settings on a style before updating it.
    *   Retrieve the exact setting names and choice values needed to reference when creating a similar style.
    *   Confirm whether a style is set as the default for its associated content type or node type.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `Key` – The unique key identifying the style to retrieve.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Show me the full details for the style with the key "HeroImageLeft"._
    *   _What settings and choices does the "CardTeaser" style have?_
    *   _Get the style details for "DefaultSection"._

`cms_create_display_template` – Creates a new style (display template) in CMS.  A style (display template) must be associated with exactly one of the following: a layout node type (for example, section, row, or column), a content base type (for example, page or component), or a specific content type.

*   **When to use**
    *   Create a new style for a specific content type, such as a hero block or article page.
    *   Add a default style for a layout node type, such as a section or row.
    *   Define a style with specific settings and choices, such as background color or image position, for editors to select in Visual Builder.
    *   Create a style that applies to all content of a given base type, such as all components or all pages.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `DisplayName` – The human-readable name of the style shown in the UI, for example, _Wide Hero_ or _Default Section_.
    *   (Optional) `Key` – Optional unique identifier for the style. If omitted, a key will be auto-generated by the server. Example: `HeroBlockWide`, `DefaultSection`.
    *   (Optional) `NodeType` – For layout node types. Valid values include: `section`, `row`, `column`. Only one of nodeType, baseType, or contentType should be provided.
    *   (Optional) `BaseType` – For content base types. Valid values: `_page`, `_component`, `_media`, `_image`, `_video`, `_folder`, `_experience`, `_section`, `_element`. Only one of nodeType, baseType, or contentType should be provided.
    *   (Optional) `ContentType` – For specific content types, for example, `HeroBlock`, `ArticlePage`. Only one of nodeType, baseType, or contentType should be provided.
    *   (Optional) `IsDefault` – Whether this style is the default for its associated type. Defaults to false.
    *   (Optional) `Settings` – Settings for the style as a JSON object. Each setting can have choices that users can select from. Setting fields: `displayName` (required), `editor` (optional), `sortOrder` (optional), `choices` (optional dictionary of `{ displayName, sortOrder }`).
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Create a style called "Wide Hero" for the HeroBlock content type with a background color setting that has light and dark choices._
    *   _Add a default style for the section node type called "Default Section"._
    *   _Create a new style for all components called "Rounded Corners" with the key "ComponentRounded"._
    *   _Set up a style for ArticlePage with an image position setting that lets editors choose between left and right._

`cms_update_display_template` – Updates an existing style (display template) in CMS. Only the provided fields are updated; all other fields remain unchanged. When settings are provided, they replace all existing settings entirely. Any existing settings not included in the update will be removed. Include all desired settings in a single call.

*   **When to use**
    *   Rename an existing style without changing its settings or type association.
    *   Set a style as the default for its associated content type or node type.
    *   Update or replace the settings and choices on an existing style.
    *   Change the content type or node type a style is associated with.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `Key` – The unique key of the style to update. Example: `HeroBlockWide`, `DefaultSection`.
    *   (Optional) `DisplayName` – The human-readable name of the style shown in the UI, for example, `Wide Hero` or `Default Section`.
    *   (Optional) `NodeType` – For layout node types. Valid values include: `section`, `row`, `column`.
    *   (Optional) `BaseType` – For content base types. Valid values: `_page`, `_component`, `_media`, `_image`, `_video`, `_folder`, `_experience`, `_section`, `_element`'.
    *   (Optional) `ContentType` – For specific content types, for example, `HeroBlock`, `ArticlePage`.
    *   (Optional) `IsDefault` – Whether this style is the default for its associated type.
    *   (Optional) `Settings` – Settings for the style as a JSON object. Each setting can have choices that users can select from. Setting fields: `displayName` (required), `editor` (optional), `sortOrder` (optional), `choices` (optional dictionary of `{ displayName, sortOrder }`).
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Rename the "HeroBlockWide" style to "Extra Wide Hero"._
    *   _Set the "CardTeaser" style as the default for its content type._
    *   _Update the settings on the "HeroImageLeft" style to add a new theme choice called "Dark"._
    *   _Replace the background color choices on the "DefaultSection" style with white, gray, and black._

*   **When to use**
    *   **For simple keyword searches** – If you need to find content items that contain a specific phrase or keyword.
    *   **When you know the content type** – If you are looking for content within a known content type, for example, _Search for 'summer sale' in 'Promotions'._
    *   **As a quick lookup** – If the `graph_content_graphql_executor` tool seems too complex or overextravagant for your immediate need.
*   **Parameters:**
    *   `searchPhrase` – The search phrase to use when searching for content.
    *   (Optional) `contentTypeName` – The specific content type to search within, for example, "Article" or "Product". If not provided, it defaults to "Data" (which might search across various types depending on configuration).
    *   (Optional) `outputFieldsAsGraphQLOutput` – The specific fields you want to retrieve for the matching content items, in GraphQL output format. If not provided, it defaults to `_fulltext`. For example, the following:
        
        "id name createdBy { id name }"
        
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Search for 'holiday promotions' in the 'Campaign' content type._
    *   _Find any 'Article' content that mentions 'customer experience' and return their titles and URLs._
    *   _What 'Product' content contains the phrase 'new features'?_
    *   _Show me all content related to 'Optimizely DXP'._

## Property groups[](#h_01K8XJ5H66WA32H2T126Y5YJ7Y)

Property groups are used to organize properties within content types, making the content editing interface more structured.

`cms_list_property_groups` – Retrieve a list of all property groups available in CMS (SaaS). This tool returns raw JSON data.

*   **When to use**
    *   See all existing property groups in your instance of CMS (SaaS).
    *   Identify available groups to use when creating or updating content types with the `cms_create_content_type` tool or `cms_update_content_type` tool.
    *   Determine if a new property group needs to be created before defining new content type properties.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `IncludeSystemGroups` – Indicates whether pre-built property groups from the 'system' source should be included in the results. 
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all property groups in my CMS (SaaS) instance._
    *   _Show me the available property groups._
    *   _Are there any property groups for 'SEO'?_
    *   _Include system groups when listing property groups._

`cms_create_property_group` – Create a property group used for content type properties in CMS (SaaS). Group names should be short, concise, and indicative of their use.
